title: Evaluation context (the policy-engine interface)
description: The transient shared space a request evaluation creates, which policies read from and write to across passes (policy-contract §7.1). This is THE INTERFACE: under ADR-065 the engine is a black box, so the context shape is one of the few things that must be exact for two implementations to interoperate. It is transient — never persisted as entity data — but the snapshot at each pass is captured in the audit record, which is the form this schema governs. Not a record: it has no uuid identity, no lifecycle, and no version of its own; it belongs to the request evaluation that created it.

request_uuid.description: The request evaluation this context belongs to. RFC 9562 v4.

pass_number.description: Which evaluation pass produced this snapshot. Re-entrant evaluation (§7.2, ADR-006) means the same policy may contribute across passes; the pass number is what makes an accumulated constraint attributable to a moment rather than to the set.

max_passes.description: The convergence bound for this evaluation. An ENGINE PARAMETER set by the implementation, not by the contract (§7.2a) — carried here so an audit snapshot records the bound that was in force, not so UDLM prescribes one.

constraints.description: Constraints emitted by policies, accumulating across passes. Each carries provenance because conflict resolution is only possible when a constraint can be attributed — a constraint whose source is unknown cannot be weighed against another, overridden, or explained in an audit.

constraint_uuid.description: Identity of this constraint within the evaluation. RFC 9562 v4.

source_policy.description: The policy that emitted it — the WHO of provenance. Required: an unattributable constraint cannot be resolved against a conflicting one.

source_domain.description: The domain the emitting policy belongs to — the precedence axis (§4). Required for the same reason: precedence cannot be applied to a constraint whose domain is unknown.

constraint_type.description: Which accumulator this constraint contributes to — a canonical term in the `evaluation-context` subtree of the policy-fact taxonomy (registry/taxonomies/policy-fact.yaml), enforced by tests/check_policy_facts.py. This is the round-trip the evaluation context exists for: what a policy EMITS under a name is what a later policy READS as a fact under that same name (`allowed_zones` emitted, `allowed_zones` read). One name for the two directions — governing it is what keeps them from drifting apart.

field.description: The dot-path this constraint targets within the accumulator, when narrower than the accumulator itself (e.g. `placement.zone_distribution`). Optional: a constraint may apply to the accumulator as a whole.

operator.description: How the constraint applies. This is EMISSION, not comparison — what a policy produces, which is UDLM's side of the contract (ADR-065 keeps the decision and constraint shapes). A policy compares facts in its engine's language, then emits a constraint in this one.

value.description: The constraint's payload — a zone set, a ceiling, a distribution rule. Untyped here because its shape follows constraint_type.

binding.description: hard = cannot be overridden by a later pass or a lower-precedence domain; soft = a preference. Required: whether a constraint can be relaxed is not a detail a resolver may infer.

reason.description: Human-readable justification, surfaced in the conflict report when evaluation cannot converge.

pass_added.description: Which pass emitted it — the WHEN of provenance, and what makes convergence auditable rather than merely asserted.

hints.description: Advisory signals flowing between policies within an evaluation. EPHEMERAL — never persisted as entity data (§7.1). A hint carries no binding and cannot constrain; a policy that needs to bind emits a constraint instead.

from_policy.description: The policy that offered the hint.

to_concern.description: The concern_type the hint is addressed to (placement, security, compliance …) — hints are routed by concern, not to a named policy, so a hint survives the addressee being replaced.

hint_type.description: What kind of signal this is.

resolutions.description: How conflicts were handled. The record that makes convergence explainable: §7.2 requires a full conflict report when evaluation cannot converge, and this is what that report is assembled from.

strategy.description: The strategy applied, from the emitting policy's on_conflict declaration.

resolved_by.description: Who resolved it. `human` and `escalation` are recorded, never elided — a decision that left the machine is the one an auditor most needs to find.

resolved_constraints.description: The settled constraint set downstream policies and placement consume — the accumulator's value once the pass completes. Derived from `constraints` (DRV-001): carried in an audit snapshot because recomputing it later would require replaying the evaluation, not because it is an independent fact.

constraints.reason: eu_personal data may only be realized in an EU sovereignty zone
